entries.message: This update includes review and repair alternate-order history conflicts and harden sync, history recovery and selected episode ordering.
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Manual episode actions use the selected TVDB order when saving new watches.
Earlier watches with uncertain episode identity appear in Manual Watch review with aired and selected-order candidates.
An administrator confirms the intended episode before Plekt repairs history after verifying a local backup.
Force Sync of an already-synced title no longer removes a Trakt play without adding it back.
Added users no longer share a show identity cache, Seerr status cache, scheduler guard, dispatch sweep flag or live-change prune timer.
Unwatches and duplicate watches need stronger evidence, so a partly watched Plex item or an Emby-only watch is no longer changed on thin evidence.
A partial or failed provider read for Plex watchlists, playlists, resume feeds or Jellyfin watched scans is no longer treated as a complete one.
A throwing lease renewal or scheduled job still schedules the next run, and a stalled response body now stops at the configured timeout.
Old session cookies stop working for a re-created user, an administrator password reset signs the user out, and repeated slashes no longer skip rate limits.
The cloud metadata block also catches trailing dots, IPv4-mapped and NAT64 IPv6 forms and more metadata addresses.
Testing a Plex notification or Tautulli connection with a different URL now needs its own token or key instead of reusing the saved one.
Keep watched episodes on their selected DVD or alternate-order cards when dashboard history refreshes, and clear obsolete review markers after a verified mapping.
Rebuild show progress after history restores and data wipes so restored and removed shows have current counts without a restart.
Include older watches beyond the newest 25,000 rows when filtering and deduplicating history.
Apply watch-date and record deletions atomically with their related playstate changes.
Retain cached cast, videos, artwork and next-airing dates during temporary metadata outages, and retry incomplete show records after five minutes.
Retry failed TVDB artwork discovery and poster downloads without leaving requests stuck or recording failures for redacted source URLs.
Use the server's local calendar day for release-date filters, next-airing dates and playlist rules, including full provider timestamps for today.
Explain that full backup restores preserve the destination machine's media and tracker connections and require reconnecting missing services.
